chapter: Laine, ragtime bands and the union
title: Papa Laine's bands and Lala joining in short pants
summary: Lala says Papa Laine hired him as a boy in short pants; Laine ran three bands, got the hot men, and played funerals.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: I had when Al Rose wanted to let him have it. Because of Italy. And Abbie played on the thing all night on the block. Where's Abbie at? Across the lake. Across the lake. We all remember Abbie, I remember Jerry and Merritt. We all started together.
Did you ever play in Papa Lane's band? No, no.
Because Lane used to come get me when I was in short pants. Yeah. That's where I started with Lane. I was in short pants. What kind of job? He's living here too. Yeah. He's still alive.
What kind of job did Lane get?
Almost every night a week. He got everything in town. He had so much, he had three bands. Number one, number two, number three. Is that right?
Where did his influence come from to get all of them?
Because he was the only one who could get hot men. See?
And he had hot bands. Yeah. Which you'd call a jazz band.

Yeah, called ragtime bands. Well we used to play funerals and everything. Funerals. Over in Gretham. Yeah, funerals. Yeah. I had me and Pop Peet and tree trumpets and all of them. I had his colored doors. I forgot his name, Italian fellas playing baritone. Playing David. Billy Scott, Dan Hughes playing the car. They were all broadfinding in those days until now. Yeah, Dan Hughes. That got to be real stiff and sopractic. Oh, that was after. That was after, huh? That was after, huh, Dan Hughes? Dan Hughes, yeah, well poor Dan didn't play. He always had men that could play. He couldn't play nothing. He was a kid, poor Dan.
